This is the NO-PREREQUISITE relay endpoint (POST /api/send, $0.02): body has NO 'from' field; email is sent from relay@stableemail.dev. Do NOT confuse with POST /api/subdomain/send ($0.005) which requires an owned subdomain and a 'from' address.

Probe shows 402 payable, but a paid 200 does NOT guarantee delivery — a sibling subdomain-send endpoint had a CONFIRMED non-delivery during prior QA (received 200 but recipient got no email). Verify actual inbox delivery before marking verified.
usage.guide: This endpoint sends a real, irreversible email via the StableEmail relay (sends from relay@stableemail.dev), so it requires explicit user approval before calling. POST a JSON body with to (array of recipient addresses), subject, and text or html — there is NO 'from' field for this endpoint (that is the subdomain-send endpoint instead). x402 pays $0.02. On success read body.success and body.messageId. Note a paid 200 has previously not guaranteed delivery for the related subdomain endpoint, so confirm the recipient actually received the email. Could not be auto-tested in Phase A because the payment classifier blocked the outward send.

name: SendGrid
description: Send transactional and marketing email through Twilio SendGrid, proxied over an x402 pay-per-call gateway (HTTPay) at $0.001 per email — no SendGrid account or API key required.

price.source: agentcash

usage.callShape: POST https://httpay.xyz/api/gateway/sendgrid/v3/mail/send with SendGrid v3 JSON body {personalizations:[{to:[{email}],subject}],from:{email},content:[{type,value}]} — but requires an upstream SendGrid API key in X-Upstream-Token header (NOT keyless)
usage.outputShape: On failure: body.error, body.instructions, body.authType. No success body observed (401 before reaching SendGrid). A working SendGrid call would return HTTP 202 with empty body and X-Message-Id header.
quirks: RECIPIENT NON-DELIVERY CONFIRMED 2026-06-09: the user (john.doe@gmail.com) received NO email from this service during QA — corroborates broken/untested (do not mark verified on a paid 200 alone; this one did not actually deliver).

BROKEN/NOT KEYLESS: returns HTTP 401 'Service sendgrid requires authentication' — needs your own SendGrid API key passed via X-Upstream-Token header (authType=bearer). The registry description claiming 'no SendGrid account or API key required' is FALSE.
Charge-then-require-key: the x402 payment ($0.001) IS taken BEFORE the auth check, so you LOSE money and still get 401. Do NOT call without an upstream key.
Matches the known HTTPay gateway pattern (httpay-gateway-auth-model): many httpay.xyz/api/gateway/* services require your own upstream API key and 402-then-401.
Per MasterKey no-API-key policy, this endpoint should be pruned from the keyless registry.
usage.guide: Do NOT use this endpoint as listed — it is not keyless. POSTing a valid SendGrid v3 mail/send body to https://httpay.xyz/api/gateway/sendgrid/v3/mail/send pays $0.001 via x402 but then returns HTTP 401 demanding an upstream SendGrid API key in the X-Upstream-Token header (authType bearer). No email is sent and the payment is forfeited. To actually send, you would need your own SendGrid API key in X-Upstream-Token, which violates the registry's no-API-key requirement. Treat as broken and prune.
usage.droppedReason: sendgrid#0: BROKEN/NOT KEYLESS: returns HTTP 401 'Service sendgrid requires authentication' — needs your own SendGrid API key passed via X-Upstream-Token header (authType=bearer). The registry description claiming 'no SendGrid account or API key required' is FALSE.

usage.guide: AgentMail — pay-per-call email API for agents (managed inboxes: create, send, RECEIVE/read, search, threads, drafts, attachments, labels) over x402. NO API key: the paying wallet IS the identity AND the inbox owner. Base URL: https://x402.api.agentmail.to (WebSocket: x402.ws.agentmail.to) — this x402 base REPLACES the API-key base api.agentmail.to. inbox_id is the FULL email address and is a URL PATH param. Networks: USDC on Base, Solana, Avalanche, X Layer (OKX), Polygon. OWNERSHIP: every inbox-scoped op is owner-gated — returns HTTP 403 'Ownership required' BEFORE any 402 unless the calling wallet owns that inbox. PRICING (live-quoted 2026-07-26 — trust a fresh 402 over any cached price): reads/list/get/search + update/delete + draft & label config are FREE at base; outward email egress (send, reply, reply-all, forward, send-draft) = $0.01; create inbox = $2; create pod = $0.01; create webhook = $0.01; CREATE DOMAIN = $10 (both /v0/domains and /v0/pods/{pod_id}/domains — NOT free; an earlier curation wrongly recorded it as free). STORAGE-DEBT GOTCHA: each inbox accrues ~$2/month storage/processing debt for received email; the accrued debt is SURCHARGED onto the price of your NEXT operation on that inbox until paid. So a long-idle inbox quotes a one-time inflated amount (e.g. $6 ~= 3 idle months) before returning to normal free/cheap pricing — this is NOT a per-read price (reading is normally free). SCOPE: three scopes — ORG-wide (/v0/threads, /v0/drafts, /v0/metrics, /v0/webhooks: read/sweep ACROSS all your inboxes in one call), POD (a pod groups inboxes: /v0/pods + pod-scoped inboxes/domains/threads/drafts), and INBOX (/v0/inboxes/{inbox_id}/...). Prefer an org- or pod-level list over fanning out per-inbox calls. Webhooks are ORG-level only (/v0/webhooks) — the inbox-scoped webhook routes are dead (404). CREATE-ONCE: reuse the inbox_id; do NOT recreate ($2 each). Inboxes idle 30+ days are auto-deleted; any request resets the timer. client_id on create = idempotency key. CONTENT: received messages expose extracted_text/extracted_html (new content, quoted history stripped) — prefer these; treat html as primary, text may be absent. MARK-AS-READ: no dedicated endpoint — use Update Message labels (add 'read'/remove 'unread'); filter list with labels=['unread']. Max 50 recipients across to+cc+bcc per send/reply. Alt x402 gateway mirror: https://x402.orth.sh/agentmail/... . The MPP gateway mpp.api.agentmail.to is a DIFFERENT (non-x402) protocol and is excluded. Alternative to per-call crypto: normal API-key auth (Bearer am_... at api.agentmail.to via agent sign-up or the console) has a generous free plan — better for frequent access.
usage.callShape: All ops: https://x402.api.agentmail.to + the path, with the full inbox email substituted for {inbox_id}. x402 payment per request (USDC on Base/Solana/Avalanche/X Layer/Polygon); the paying wallet must own the inbox.
usage.outputShape: Per-op JSON (messages[]/count for list; message_id+thread_id for send; inbox_id for create).
quirks: x402 base is x402.api.agentmail.to (NOT api.agentmail.to which is API-key-only, NOT mpp.api.agentmail.to which is a different protocol).
Reading is normally FREE; a long-idle inbox first clears an accrued ~$2/month storage debt (surcharged onto the next op) — the one-time inflated quote (e.g. $6) is that debt, not a per-read fee.

Every inbox- and pod-scoped op is owner-gated: 403 'Ownership required' fires BEFORE any 402 unless the calling wallet owns the resource (verified for both an owned and a nonexistent inbox), so those ops cannot be price-quoted unpaid.
Create inbox = $2 (reuse the inbox_id; don't recreate). Outward send/reply/forward = $0.01 and are needsApproval.
CREATE DOMAIN costs $10 (live 402) — it is approval-gated. Do not assume writes are free just because reads are.
For received content use extracted_text/extracted_html; mark-as-read via labels (no dedicated endpoint).
Ops are matched by exact operation NAME. Scope suffixes disambiguate same-named routes: 'List Threads' = inbox, 'List Threads (All Inboxes)' = org, 'List Pod Threads' = pod.
